scope_detail: Cosmian KMS 5.29.0 workspace at the head of PR #998: server, KMIP, crypto, database, HSM, clients, web UI, authentication submodule, CI/CD workflows and dependencies
methodology: STRIDE-A, CVSS 4.0 base scores, CWE, OWASP Top 10:2025
evidence_basis: Static trace of the code at the commit. F-042 and F-051 were also reproduced on a local debug build (non-FIPS, sqlite, no authentication). F-022 is a hypothesis.
severity_basis: Severity is the band of the CVSS 4.0 base score. A finding whose severity differs from that band carries base_severity_band and rating_note (raised one tier by a KMS amplifier, or capped by a documented precondition). INFO findings carry no vector.

findings.title: Auth Verifier /sessions API has no owner or realm authorisation (session-JWT theft, revocation bypass, mass logout)
findings.baseline: New (extends COSMIAN-2026-043, whose liveness check assumes the session store is trustworthy)
findings.evidence: authentication/server/src/server/auth_verifier.rs:539-552: the /sessions scope carries only CookieAuthSameServer, ExtractRealm and CORS. The scopes at :508-509, :522-523 and :554-555 add AdminAuth.

findings.title: Google CSE privilegedunwrap returns the DEK to any IdP-authenticated caller
findings.baseline: Incomplete fix and regression of COSMIAN-2025-008 (SECURITY.md:1364-1380)
findings.rating_note: ‡ Base 8.2 is HIGH. Raised one tier to CRITICAL by the key-escrow amplifier: the finding itself shows key material leaving the KMS without the key owner's consent. The independent verifier suggested HIGH
findings.evidence: crate/server/src/routes/google_cse/operations.rs:756-761,771,783-785,800-806: the request is authenticated and then cse_wrapped_key_decrypt runs as the default user with the resource name as AAD. :1175-1230 holds the shared decrypt path.

findings.title: Shipped defaults serve plain HTTP on 0.0.0.0 and treat every request as the admin user
findings.baseline: Known class (PR #998 review D1); new default-deployment angle
findings.rating_note: † Base 9.2 is CRITICAL. Capped to HIGH because this is a documented insecure default that logs a startup warning, and the operator must deploy it without configuring any authentication
findings.evidence: crate/server/src/middlewares/ensure_auth.rs:41-47 passes through an already-authenticated request. :49-55 rejects the request only when auth_is_configured. :57-59 injects AuthMethod::DefaultUser with default_username otherwise.

findings.title: Unbounded work in DeriveKey, RSA key generation and FPE pins a worker thread
findings.component: KMIP operations — DeriveKey, RSA key generation, FPE
findings.baseline: Variant of COSMIAN-2026-036. The RSA member is the residual that fix left in place

findings.evidence: crate/server/src/core/operations/create_split_key.rs:122 (part-count cap only), :129 (source bytes extracted with no size check).

findings.title: HSM keys are created extractable and non-sensitive, contradicting the documentation
findings.rating_note: ‡ Raised from MEDIUM (base 6.0) to HIGH by the HSM-boundary amplifier (+1 tier): the finding is in the HSM path and the impact is key confidentiality. With AT:N the base score would be 7.1
findings.evidence: crate/interfaces/src/hsm/hsm_store.rs:335,498 (sensitive.unwrap_or(false) and unwrap_or_default()), :346 (the key is exported from the HSM on every retrieval), :390 (a metadata-only stub is returned only for sensitive keys).

findings.title: Long-lived PAT and crates.io token exposed to workflows that run third-party code
findings.rating_note: † Capped from CRITICAL (base 9.1) to MEDIUM. The attack needs a prior compromise of a third party (a hostile release of a dependency or of a PyPI package), which this repository does not control. A reviewer who counts a hijacked dependency as in scope would keep CRITICAL
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:32 (the token has repo and workflow scopes), :103 and :281 (checkout with PAT_TOKEN), :178 (cargo build --workspace in the same job), :352 (runs a script taken from the checked-out branch).

findings.title: No CRL or OCSP revocation checking on mTLS client certificates
findings.component: TLS and mTLS client authentication (HTTPS listener and KMIP socket server)
findings.baseline: New. A documented limitation for EST only
findings.rating_note: † Capped from HIGH (base 7.6) to MEDIUM. The attack needs a client certificate or key that was already compromised and then revoked, and the limitation is documented for EST. The vector uses PR:L because the certificate belonged to a legitimate principal. With PR:N it scores 9.1
findings.evidence: crate/server/src/tls_config.rs:208 (the client CA store), :217-218 (set_verify_cert_store, SslVerifyMode::PEER: on the HTTPS listener a client certificate is optional).

findings.title: Self-hosted runner host SSH key mounted into a mutable root container (8 jobs)
findings.rating_note: † Capped from HIGH (base 7.0) to MEDIUM. The jobs run only for tags, pushes to develop and main, the schedule and manual dispatch, so exploitation needs a prior compromise of a maintainer account, of the image or of a build dependency
findings.evidence: Mount lines: .github/workflows/packaging.yml:118,229,306, packaging-apk.yml:270, packaging-kubernetes.yml:266, build_windows.yml:222, benchmark.yml:332, flamegraph.yml:112. Each job names image: cosmian/docker_doc_ci without a tag or digest (for example packaging.yml:116) and runs on [self-hosted, not-sgx] (packaging.yml:114).

findings.title: Session-key KDF uses the public URL as the password (offline test via an anonymous cookie)
findings.rating_note: † Capped to LOW. The base score is in the CRITICAL band, but the attack works only when the operator has independently chosen a guessable salt of 32 bytes or more, a failure the attacker can neither cause nor observe (AT:P). Read literally, the vector would make this CRITICAL; with VC:L/VI:L (a cookie that carries little privilege) the base is 6.3 (MEDIUM)
findings.evidence: crate/server/src/start_kms_server.rs:721-752 (salt_input at :727, password at :748), :945-953 (byte-length check), :955-958 (unreachable weak-word list), :1275-1276 (use), :1288-1293 (random key when no salt is set).

findings.title: Vault-token and login clients have no timeout or redirect policy and accept http://

The vector scores only the availability effect. Read literally, it would make this MEDIUM
findings.evidence: crate/server/src/routes/ui_auth.rs:498-500 (login client), :851-855 (logout client). crate/server/src/config/params/server_params.rs:992-998 (URL parsed, scheme not checked). Contrast: crate/server/src/middlewares/auth_verifier/session.rs:73-76.
